correctness.rationale: A finite-memory roof becomes one-letter by higher-block conjugacy. A first-mismatch argument synchronizes roof sums up to the first difference and gives a uniformly separated family of size \(p(\lfloor tn/(2M)\rfloor)\) at a fixed scale. Finite cylinders and a bounded phase mesh yield spanning sets with size at most \(K_\varepsilon p(\lceil tn/m\rceil+K_\varepsilon)\). Compact uniform continuity handles seam crossings, and the bounded-doubling condition makes all fixed linear rescalings comparable. Negative times follow time reversal. The primitive substitution \(0\mapsto0001,\ 1\mapsto0111\) has incidence eigenvalues 4,2, giving discrepancies of \(2^k\) and \(p(n)=\Theta(n)\). Its irrational two-height roof cannot be cohomologous to constant because Birkhoff discrepancies diverge. The standalone checker confirms exact finite identities but is not used as an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper expressly raises variable-roof growth preservation; this theorem settles the mathematically natural broad finite-memory subclass for all positive real roof heights and all nonzero time maps, preserving the finer growth-order invariant, not just its polynomial exponent. It has an explicit minimal, aperiodic, irrational-height and non-cohomologous example with unbounded return-time discrepancy, so it is not merely a restatement of the known constant-roof case. The proof supplies genuinely quantitative spanning and separated bounds; arbitrary continuous roofs are deliberately excluded.
